outcome.answer: Yes—under certain setups, standard (message-passing) GNNs can perform zero-shot link prediction on unknown/unseen knowledge graphs. In particular, reifying the input graph into a node-based representation and then applying “textbook” GNNs lets five vanilla GNNs (including GAT, R-GCN, and GraphSAGE variants) transfer zero-shot to 40 inductive link-prediction benchmarks, matching a dedicated KG foundation model on its evaluation suite in the authors’ experiments [1].
